references.text: God's command that the people of Israel be holy because the Lord their God is holy, which is the basis for the priests' holiness.
The priests must keep away from the holy offerings of the Israelites so they do not profane God's holy name.
Description of a fire offering as food for the Lord, linked to the expression 'the bread of his God' in the verse.
The priest shall be holy because he presents the bread of his God, a direct parallel to the theme of the priest's holiness.
The expression 'the bread of his God' is used again regarding the offerings that the priests present.
Another reference to 'the bread of his God' in connection with priestly service at the altar.
A fire offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord, describing the type of offering the priests were to present.
The Lord's offering is described as his food, a fire offering with a pleasing aroma, parallel to 'the bread of the Lord'.
Prophetic warning that God's holy name was profaned among the nations, showing the seriousness of profaning His name.
Believers as a holy priesthood presenting spiritual offerings, a New Testament fulfillment of priestly holiness.
Believers as a royal priesthood and a holy nation, extending the Old Testament priestly calling to all believers.
